previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with a history of cholangiocarcinoma and recurrent cholangitis, was admitted with fever, nausea, and a loose bowel movement following completion of a prior antibiotic course. Initial evaluation revealed stable vital signs, no growth in blood cultures, and imaging showing persistent cholangitis in the right intrahepatic bile ducts on MRCP, with no evidence of pneumonia. He was started on meropenem, but due to worsening pancytopenia, was switched to ertapenem. An ERCP was performed, confirming sludge in the biliary stents, which was cleared, though access to the right intrahepatic system was not achieved. A new PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic administration. He remained afebrile, clinically improved, and was discharged home on a 12-day course of IV ertapenem followed by oral delafloxacin for suppressive therapy, with plans for weekly lab monitoring and follow-up with infectious disease and gastroenterology.
